Container.Name: beacon-uptime
Container.Overview:
Open-source uptime monitoring: HTTP/TCP/DNS/SSL/Ping/Heartbeat monitors, public status pages, incident management, and multi-channel alerting (email, Slack, Discord, webhooks).
This all-in-one image runs the whole stack in one container: an embedded PostgreSQL 16 + TimescaleDB database, a loopback-only Redis, the dashboard/API, the BullMQ worker and the scheduler, supervised together. All state (the database and a self-generated secrets file) lives in the one /data share — back that folder up and you've backed up the install.
First boot generates the session secret and the embedded database's password automatically; no secret needs to be typed to get a working install. Register the first account at the web UI to get started.
For access beyond your LAN, put a reverse-proxy in front (Nginx Proxy Manager or SWAG both work) and set the Base URL below to your public https address — Beacon builds every absolute link (status pages, alert emails, incident links) from that value.
To use an external Postgres or Redis instead of the embedded ones, fill in the optional Database URL / Redis URL fields (advanced) — leaving them blank uses the embedded services. An external database must have the TimescaleDB extension available; migrations fail fast if it doesn't.
Container.Requires: None for a default install — the embedded database and cache need nothing external. A reverse proxy is only required for access beyond your LAN.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the dashboard, API and status pages (all served on this one port). 3410 was verified free on this box.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: All state: the embedded PostgreSQL data directory and the auto-generated secrets file (session secret + database password). Back this folder up; losing it loses every monitor, status page and account.

Config.Name: Base URL
Config.Description: The public address users and links point to — used to build status page URLs, alert-email links, and incident links. Set this to your reverse-proxy's https hostname before inviting anyone. ⚠ The session cookie is always marked Secure in this image, so sign-in only works over https: reach the install through this hostname (behind a TLS-terminating proxy), not by hitting the bare LAN IP over http.

Config.Name: BREVO_API_KEY
Config.Description: Optional: API key for Brevo (Sendinblue) — sends alert emails and subscriber notifications. Leave blank to disable outbound email; monitoring, the dashboard and the API all still work without it.

Config.Name: FROM_EMAIL
Config.Description: Optional: the From: address on alert and subscriber emails. Only matters if BREVO_API_KEY is set.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: Optional: point at an external PostgreSQL instead of the embedded one (postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db). It MUST have the TimescaleDB extension available — migrations fail fast if it doesn't. Leave blank to use the embedded database in /data.

Config.Name: REDIS_URL
Config.Description: Optional: point at an external Redis instead of the embedded loopback one (redis://[:password@]host:6379). Leave blank to use the embedded Redis.

Config.Name: PROBE_REGION
Config.Description: Optional: a region label attached to check results — cosmetic unless you run several instances and compare regions.

Config.Name: ALLOW_REGISTRATION
Config.Description: Registration is open only until the first account exists; that person owns the install. Set to true to let more people sign up (anyone who can reach the URL).

Config.Name: DATA_RETENTION_DAYS
Config.Description: Optional: days of raw check results kept before cleanup. Hourly/daily uptime aggregates are kept for a year regardless.
